landing.faq.what_is.question: What is CurvG AI, and how does it use Manim?
landing.faq.what_is.answer: CurvG is an independent creation tool built around Manim Community, the open-source Python engine for mathematical animation. It turns a written explanation goal into a scene plan and Manim code, with a review step before rendering.
landing.faq.installation.question: Do I need Python, FFmpeg, or LaTeX installed locally?
landing.faq.installation.answer: No local setup is required to plan a scene or generate code in CurvG. To run the code on your own computer, you still need a compatible Manim environment. In-product video rendering is available only when a renderer is configured.
landing.faq.editing.question: Can I edit and compile the generated Manim code in the browser?
landing.faq.editing.answer: Not yet. The current Creator lets you view, copy, and download generated Python, but it does not provide direct code editing or compilation in the browser.
landing.faq.free.question: Can I use CurvG AI for free?
landing.faq.free.answer: Yes. Free and Starter can use Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5, and Gemini 3.1 Pro through Kie. Pro unlocks all seven curated models.
landing.faq.difference.question: How is CurvG different from a one-click AI video generator?
landing.faq.difference.answer: CurvG does not stop at a prompt and a final video. It shows the proposed explanation, mathematical assumptions, scene order, and generated Manim code, so you can catch a problem before rendering. AI output is still not guaranteed to be correct.
landing.faq.accuracy.question: Can AI guarantee a mathematically correct animation?
landing.faq.accuracy.answer: No. A model can misread notation, make a false assumption, or generate incorrect scene logic. CurvG makes those decisions easier to inspect, but it does not replace mathematical review.
landing.faq.rendering.question: Is remote Manim rendering live in production?
landing.faq.rendering.answer: Yes, hosted rendering is configured in production. Paid plans include render credits; Free still lets you generate, review, copy, and download Manim code without included hosted-render credits.

landing.pricing.faq.title: What to expect before you upgrade
landing.pricing.faq.description: A short, factual guide to Free, Starter, Pro, generated code, billing, and hosted rendering.
landing.pricing.faq.free.question: What is included in the Free plan?
landing.pricing.faq.free.answer: Free includes scene planning, generated Manim code, and three curated models. You can review, copy, and download code, but Free does not include hosted-render credits.
landing.pricing.faq.pro.question: How do Starter and Pro differ?
landing.pricing.faq.pro.answer: On monthly billing, Starter includes three curated models and 300 render credits; Pro includes all seven models, automatic Kie model fallback, and 1,000 credits. Annual billing grants 3,600 or 12,000 credits for the year. AI output still needs review.
landing.pricing.faq.billing.question: Are Starter and Pro subscriptions?
landing.pricing.faq.billing.answer: Yes. Both have monthly and yearly billing. Manage or cancel an active plan from Settings → Billing; cancellation stops the next renewal.
landing.pricing.faq.code.question: Can I use the generated Manim code outside CurvG?
landing.pricing.faq.code.answer: Yes. You can copy or download the generated Python code. Running it on your own computer still requires a compatible Manim environment and any dependencies used by the scene.
landing.pricing.faq.rendering.question: How are hosted renders calculated?
landing.pricing.faq.rendering.answer: The current standard render costs 20 credits. That makes 300 credits about 15 renders and 1,000 credits about 50. Failed or canceled renders are refunded; estimates can change if the configured render cost changes.
landing.footer.disclaimer: Manim is an open-source project maintained by the Manim Community. CurvG AI is an independent product and is not affiliated with the Manim Community or 3Blue1Brown.
